title: Amazon jumps as AWS growth soothes fears over its AI spending
excerpt: Amazon shares jumped more than 12% after its cloud division posted its fastest growth in over four years, easing investor fears that the company’s ballooning AI spending was running ahead of the payoff. Amazon Web Services grew 37% in the
content_html:
Amazon shares jumped more than 12% after its cloud division posted its fastest growth in over four years, easing investor fears that the company’s ballooning AI spending was running ahead of the payoff.

Amazon Web Services grew 37% in the second quarter, well past the roughly 31% analysts expected, adding something like $300bn to Amazon’s market value before the bell.

It was a sharp turn from the previous quarter, when a one-off Anthropic gain flattered the numbers and free cash flow collapsed.

AWS is the engine once more. The unit brought in $42.2bn in the quarter and reaccelerated to a pace it had not touched since the last cloud boom, reassuring a market that had grown nervous about the cost of AI.

The worry it soothed was specific. Investors have spent the year asking whether the hyperscalers are pouring hundreds of billions into data centres faster than customers will pay for the capacity.

Amazon’s answer was that demand is outrunning supply. Chief executive Andy Jassy said demand was so strong that the company’s computing capacity was not enough to serve customers, even after it raised its spending.

That spending is enormous. Amazon lifted its planned capital expenditure about 10% to roughly $220bn, one of the largest build-out budgets in corporate history, most of it aimed at AI and cloud.

The bill is showing up in cash flow. Free cash flow swung to negative $7.6bn on a trailing-twelve-month basis, down from a positive $18.2bn a year earlier, a reminder that the AI race is being paid for in real money.

Amazon has been funding it aggressively. The company has taken on billions in fresh debt to keep the data-centre build going, part of a wider borrowing spree across Big Tech.

The market decided the growth was worth it. At least five brokerages raised their price targets, focusing on the reacceleration in AWS rather than the cash outflow.

Analysts tied the two together. “We’re encouraged by the strength in the core AWS business, which has a high correlation with AI revenue,” JP Morgan wrote, arguing the link between cloud growth and AI will only tighten.

The result reframes a season of nerves. Big Tech’s combined capex has blown past $600bn, and each earnings report has become a referendum on whether that money is translating into revenue.

Amazon’s peers have faced the same test. Meta recently raised the floor on its AI spending even as its cash flow tightened, and Microsoft and Alphabet have leaned on cloud growth to justify their own outlays.

The read-through is sector-wide. With Microsoft, Alphabet, and now Amazon all pointing to cloud demand they cannot fully meet, the mood has shifted from questioning the spending to asking whether there is enough capacity to go around.

The comparison flatters Amazon for now. Its shares trade at a higher earnings multiple than Microsoft’s or Alphabet’s, a sign investors are willing to pay up for the growth AWS is showing.

There is a hardware story underneath. Amazon has been pushing its own custom AI chips, which Jassy has suggested could become a business worth tens of billions, giving it a lever on the costs that squeeze rivals.

The strategy is vertical integration at scale. By building chips, data centres, and cloud services together, Amazon is betting it can serve AI demand more cheaply than competitors who buy their silicon from Nvidia.

The risk has not vanished, only receded. If AWS growth slows again while capex stays near $220bn, the same cash-flow questions will return, and the market’s patience could prove thin.

For this quarter, though, Jassy got the number he needed. A reaccelerating cloud business is the clearest evidence Amazon can offer that its AI bet is being met with demand, not just hope.

content_html_zh:
亚马逊云部门录得四年多来最快增长后，亚马逊股价上涨逾 12%，缓解了投资者对该公司不断膨胀的人工智能支出超出回报的担忧。

亚马逊网络服务第二季度增长了 37%，远远超出了分析师大约 31% 的预期，亚马逊盘前市值增加了约 3000 亿美元。

与上一季度相比，这是一个急剧的转变，当时一次性的人为收益使数字变得美化，自由现金流崩溃。

AWS 再次成为引擎。 该部门本季度收入达 422 亿美元，并重新加速到自上次云繁荣以来从未达到的速度，安抚了对人工智能成本日益紧张的市场。

它所缓解的担忧是具体的。 投资者一年来一直在询问超大规模企业向数据中心投入数千亿美元的资金是否比客户为容量支付的速度要快。

亚马逊的答案是供不应求。 首席执行官安迪·贾西 (Andy Jassy) 表示，需求如此强劲，以至于公司的计算能力不足以为客户提供服务，即使在增加支出之后也是如此。

这笔支出是巨大的。 亚马逊将计划资本支出提高约 10%，达到约 2200 亿美元，这是公司历史上最大的扩建预算之一，其中大部分针对人工智能和云。

该账单显示在现金流量中。 过去 12 个月的自由现金流从一年前的正 182 亿美元降至负 76 亿美元，这提醒人们，人工智能竞赛是用真金白银支付的。

亚马逊一直在积极为其提供资金。 该公司已承担了数十亿美元的新债务，以维持数据中心建设的顺利进行，这是整个大型科技公司更广泛借贷热潮的一部分。

市场认为这种增长是值得的。 至少有五家券商提高了价格目标，重点关注 AWS 的重新加速，而不是现金流出。

分析师将两者联系在一起。 摩根大通写道：“我们对核心 AWS 业务的实力感到鼓舞，该业务与人工智能收入高度相关。”他认为云增长与人工智能之间的联系只会更加紧密。

结果重新塑造了一个令人紧张的赛季。 大型科技公司的资本支出合计已超过 6000 亿美元，每一份收益报告都成为对这些资金是否转化为收入的全民公投。

亚马逊的同行也面临着同样的考验。 Meta 最近提高了其人工智能支出的下限，尽管其现金流收紧，而微软和 Alphabet 则依靠云增长来证明自己的支出合理。

通读范围是整个行业。 随着微软、Alphabet 和现在的亚马逊都指出他们无法完全满足云需求，人们的情绪已经从质疑支出转变为询问是否有足够的容量来满足。

目前，这种比较让亚马逊感到很高兴。 其股价的市盈率高于微软或 Alphabet 的市盈率，这表明投资者愿意为 AWS 的增长付出代价。

下面有一个硬件故事。 亚马逊一直在推出自己的定制人工智能芯片，贾西表示，这可能会成为一项价值数百亿美元的业务，从而使其在成本上有优势，从而挤压竞争对手。

该战略是大规模的垂直整合。 亚马逊相信，通过共同构建芯片、数据中心和云服务，它能够比从英伟达购买芯片的竞争对手更便宜地满足人工智能需求。

风险并没有消失，只是减弱了。 如果 AWS 增长再次放缓，而资本支出保持在 2200 亿美元附近，同样的现金流问题将会再次出现，市场的耐心可能会减弱。

不过，在本季度，贾西得到了他需要的数字。 云业务的重新加速是亚马逊可以提供的最明确的证据，表明其人工智能赌注正在满足需求，而不仅仅是希望。
